title: FragileFlip primer and quiet-escape log
content:
Purpose:
- Scratchpad for the FragileFlip (FF) launch: small, risky model flip for a routing-sensitive endpoint. Personal notes, TODOs, and an escape/quiet-rollback strategy.

High-level goal:
- Flip model v2.3.1 -> v2.4-quant in controlled cohorts to measure latency and quality delta while keeping cost impact bounded. Give product teams a safety-first path to enable v2.4 progressively.

MVP success criteria (quick):
1) No increase in p95 latency > 40ms on baseline routes for 95% of requests in canary window.
2) Error rate (5xx + inference fails) <= baseline + 0.1%.
3) Quality checks: eval prompts (canary set) BLEU/ROUGE-style anchor shows <= 2% regressions and no repeat hallucination pattern for top 50 prompts.

Canary cohorts (sequence):
- Phase A (quiet probe, 30m): 0.05% traffic, internal-first (platform, staging clients). Aim: catch immediate runtime errors, memory OOMs, small latency blips.
- Phase B (soft warmup, 2h): 0.5% traffic, alpha customers flagged as "fragileflip-probe". Monitor token-cost, KV cache hit rates.
- Phase C (gradual growth, 6h): 2% -> 5% traffic ramp if metrics stable. Include a second region (eu-west-1) to ensure cross-region kernel selection behaves.
- Phase D (broader soak, 24h): 10% traffic only if Phase C passes sustained checks.

Warmup and priming notes:
- Warm KV cache by replaying recent stable prefixes from identical traffic shape (see linked artifact PR/2789 for loader).
- Warmup cohort should receive same model config (quantization flags) as final rollout; avoid mixing quant setups in early probe.
- Pre-load static prompts (login flow, top 50 queries) into prefix cache to reduce cold-start noise in first 30 minutes.

Pinning strategy:
- Edge clients: use per-client pin map for first 24h. Pin map TTL = 1h, then increase to 6h if stable.
- For clients without SDK pinning, route by tenant header -> use routing table to force v2.3.1 unless in explicit FF cohort.
- Backfill mapping: we will regenerate assignment tokens for warm cohorts every 30m to avoid accidental long-lived pins.

Quiet-escape (soft rollback) concept (unique to this flip):
- Rather than instant global rollback, we do a "quiet-escape" in two steps to avoid noisy thrashing:
  1) Quiet-redirect: silently reroute 90% of affected cohort traffic back to v2.3.1 but keep 10% as a golden probe for debugging (no client-visible changes). This limits impact while preserving signal.
  2) Controlled pin purge: after 10 minutes of quiet-redirect (verify p95/p99 normal), purge cohort pins and mark clients as warmed for v2.3.1.
- Why: instant rollback sometimes causes surges and cache churn; quiet-redirect reduces churning within cluster while protecting users.

Rollback triggers (automated + manual):
- Automated thresholds (anyone: SRE auto-fires):
  - p95 increased > 100ms vs baseline for 3 continuous 1-minute windows.
  - Error rate > baseline + 0.5% sustained 5 minutes.
  - Token-cost spike > 40% unexplained (check batch sizes / kernel fallback).
  - Regression monitors on eval prompts show > 5% regression on quality metric or new hallucination cluster.
- Manual triggers:
  - Product or CS calls out reproducible customer regressions.
  - Security/PII detection on new model variant.

Telemetry checklist (what I will watch on the dashboard):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 per route, and aggregated. Watch tail (p99) per-customer.
- Errors: 4xx/5xx trending and inference-specific errors (OOM, kernel-fallback).
- Cost: tokens/req, tokens/hour, GPU-seconds per route.
- Cache: KV cache hit rate, prefix-hit ratio, cold-start percent.
- Quality: regression eval set pass/fail (rolling window), top-50 prompt diffs, token-level perplexity shift.
- Deployment signals: rollout fraction, cohort list, pinned clients count, pin TTL distribution.

Operational runbook (quick commands & owners):
- Quick revert (quiet-redirect): infra-runbooks/quiet-redirect.sh --cohort "fragileflip-A" --to-version v2.3.1 --fraction 0.9 (SRE + owner sign-off).
- Hard rollback (global): deploy-manager rollback --service inference --target v2.3.1 (requires on-call + ENG lead).
- Cache warm reload: tools/kv-preload --source recent-prefixes --cohort fragileflip-A (DevEx/Evan).

Client & Partner comms (todo):
- Short ping to alpha clients in Phase B explaining small probe and escape plan. Keep message short, include opt-out instructions. (Owner: Maya)
- Internal Slack channel #fragileflip with pinned watchlist and escalation contacts (include SRE lead, product PM).

Known risks / open questions (needs follow-up):
- Quantized kernel fallback behavior in eu-west-1 sometimes selects CPU path for some layer types — verify with infra team (ticket noted in PR/2789).
- Does function-calling change require new safety checks for v2.4? Product says no, but verify with safety-runbook.
- Impact on per-token billing for customers with metered plans — need finance note if cost delta > 10%.

Post-mortem anchors (what to capture if we hit regression):
- Timeline: exact minute-by-minute routing changes and cohort assignments.
- Heap traces / kernel fallback logs for any OOMs.
- Diff sample sets (top 200 queries) between v2.3.1 and v2.4 to pinpoint behavioral regressions.
- Cost delta analysis: tokens, GPU secs, and per-request latency.

Small TODOs (me):
- [ ] Add alpha client opt-out template and ask Maya to send.
- [ ] Confirm quiet-redirect script args with SRE (Evan).
- [ ] Add the warmup loader config into PR/2789 and link it here.
- [ ] Check conda/pip env for local reproduce (I keep hitting different quant kernels locally).
- [ ] Bake a one-pager for CS that explains quiet-escape (2 paragraphs).

Notes-to-self (random):
- Keep the golden 10% probe for at least 30 minutes during quiet-redirect to capture intermittent faults.
- If we see a tiny p99 spike but all else OK, hold and re-evaluate rather than immediate purge — p99 is noisy.
- Lean on per-tenant history rather than aggregate for rollback decisions; a single high-value tenant >50% of failures should drive manual rollback.

End of scratchpad.

Revision history:
- 2026-03-05: Draft initial plan and canary cohorts.
- 2026-03-08: Added quiet-escape steps after discussion with Evan.
- 2026-03-12: Updated rollback thresholds and added warmup checklist.
